Ezekiel 19 · A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: The Most High tells Ezekiel to take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel, asking what is thy mother, a lioness that lay down among lions and nourished her whelps among young lions.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: One of her whelps became a young lion that learned to catch the prey and devoured men, picturing how a particular leader devoured his own people.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: The nations heard of him, took him in their pit, and brought him with chains unto the land of Egypt, showing that when the leader is judged he is dragged off into captivity.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: When the mother saw her hope was lost she took another of her whelps and made him a young lion, and he too learned to catch the prey and devoured men.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: He knew their desolate places, laid waste their cities, and left the land desolate by the noise of his roaring, so the nations set against him on every side and spread their net over him.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: The judgment is that the Most High always sends the sword, and the sword is the nations; they came up and set a net and a trap all around Jerusalem so there was no escape.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: They put him in a ward and chains and brought him to the king of Babylon, so he is no longer roaring like a lion but sits chained in Babylon.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: The mother is likened to a vine planted by the waters, fruitful and full of branches, with strong rods for the scepters of them that bear rule, exalted among the thick branches.

note.label: Ezekiel 19: A Lamentation for the Princes of Israel

points: But she was plucked up in fury and cast down to the ground, meaning cast down from rulership, and the east wind, which is judgment, dried up her fruit.

Her strong rods were broken and withered and the fire consumed them, and now she is planted in the wilderness in a dry and thirsty ground with no strong rod left to be a scepter to rule; this is the lamentation.
